title: Continuum: Efficient and Robust Multi-Turn LLM Agent Scheduling with KV Cache Time-to-Live
venue: arXiv 2511.02230 (cs.OS); later ICLR 2026 listing seen only in search
quote: tool-call pauses "prevent effective KV reuse across turns"
proves: End-of-turn eviction breaks agentic workloads; a per-request KV TTL that keeps KV in GPU memory during tool calls, plus program-level FCFS, cuts average job completion time by over 8x (SWE-Bench, BFCL; Llama-3.1 8B/70B).
does_not_prove: Datacenter GPU setting; TTL weighs recompute/reload vs memory but not on unified memory or with OS memory pressure; no small-model or laptop study.
bearing: threatens: TTL/pause-aware retention as a new idea; supports: porting pause-aware retention to unified memory

title: KVFlow: Efficient Prefix Caching for Accelerating LLM-Based Multi-Agent Workflows
quote: which fails to anticipate future agent usage and often discards KV caches shortly before their reuse
proves: LRU prefix eviction is wrong for multi-agent workflows; steps-to-execution scores from an agent step graph drive eviction and CPU-to-GPU prefetch; up to 1.83x (single workflow) and 2.19x (many concurrent) over SGLang hierarchical radix cache.
does_not_prove: Needs a known workflow graph; prefetch assumes a separate CPU tier, which does not exist on unified memory.
bearing: threatens: workflow-aware prefix eviction; supports: graph-free or unified-memory variants

title: TokenCake: A KV-Cache-centric Serving Framework for LLM-based Multi-Agent Applications
venue: arXiv 2510.18586; comments say accepted at EuroSys '27
quote: temporal underutilization leaves the cache of agents stalled on long-running function calls idling in GPU memory
proves: Offloads idle KV during function calls and predictively uploads before tool completion; up to 47.06% lower end-to-end latency in memory-constrained settings, +16.9 pp effective GPU utilization vs vLLM.
does_not_prove: Offload target is CPU DRAM over PCIe; on Apple unified memory offload means SSD or compression, not a different memory pool.
bearing: threatens: offload-during-tool-call; supports: SSD/compress-during-pause on laptops

title: InferCept: Efficient Intercept Support for Augmented Large Language Model Inference
quote: unnecessary recomputation of already computed contexts, which accounts for 37-40% of total model forwarding time
proves: Treating each tool interception as end of generation wastes 37-40% of forward time; adaptive preserve/discard/swap gives 1.6x-2x serving throughput.
does_not_prove: Continuum (F1) says InferCept assumes predictable tool durations; GPU+CPU swap setting only.
bearing: threatens: preserve/discard/swap choice at pauses (well studied)

title: CacheWise: Understanding Workloads and Optimizing KVCache Management for Efficiently Serving LLM Coding Agents
quote: Our analysis shows that coding agent sessions repeatedly reuse large prefixes and create sustained KVCache pressure
proves: Real coding-assistant traces show long closed-loop sessions alternating generation and tool calls with sustained KV pressure; CacheWise cuts KV evictions 2-2.6x and session completion time up to 3.5x.
does_not_prove: Abstract does not give per-turn numbers I could verify; datacenter setting.
bearing: threatens: agent-aware eviction on servers; supports: trace-driven replay for local agents

title: TraceLab: Characterizing Coding Agent Workloads for LLM Serving (blog + paper)
quote: Rounds that start from a new user message fare much worse, hitting only **~84.4%**
proves: Claude Code / Codex traces: 95.7% of input tokens hit cache overall, ~97.5% after tool calls, ~84.4% after a new user message; ~4% of tool calls last over a minute and take ~85% of tool time; retention break-even across user pauses is left open.
does_not_prove: Hit rates are provider-side with provider TTLs; does not measure what a local engine with tight memory would see.
bearing: supports: retention across human-paced gaps as an open question; threatens: claims that agent prefix hit rate is low

title: Agentic Coding in the Wild: Characterizing GitHub Copilot at Production Scale
quote: KV cache hit rates averaging 90% within a turn, but falling to 55% across turn boundaries
proves: Production Copilot agent traffic: 90% within-turn KV hit vs 55% across turn boundaries; caches drastically invalidated by model switches or context compaction; an idle-time predictor captures 86-90% of idle time.
does_not_prove: Only the abstract page was read; mechanism of loss across turns (TTL vs eviction vs compaction) not separated here.
bearing: supports: cross-turn retention and compaction-aware caching gaps

title: R-KV: Redundancy-aware KV Cache Compression for Reasoning Models
quote: preserves nearly 100% of the full KV cache performance using only 10% of the KV cache
proves: Long reasoning outputs break prompt-oriented compression (reasoning failures); redundancy-aware decode-time compression keeps ~100% accuracy at 10% KV.
does_not_prove: Accuracy-focused; NeurIPS and arXiv numbers differ per search; not evaluated inside a paged serving engine with batching on Apple hardware.
bearing: threatens: decode-time KV compression for reasoning (crowded)

title: Hold Onto That Thought: Assessing KV Cache Compression On Reasoning
quote: eviction strategies at low budgets can produce longer reasoning traces
proves: Benchmark: prefill-oriented methods are rarely tested on long decode; H2O and a decode-enabled SnapKV dominate for reasoning; low budgets lengthen traces (more decode steps).
does_not_prove: Does not measure end-to-end serving time, so the net effect of longer traces vs smaller KV is open.
bearing: supports: measuring cache budget vs trace length tradeoff end to end; negative result for naive eviction

title: ThinKV: Thought-Adaptive KV Cache Compression for Efficient Reasoning Models
quote: we design a kernel that extends PagedAttention to enable efficient reuse of evicted tokens' memory slots,
proves: Thought-type-aware quantize+evict with a PagedAttention extension reusing freed slots; near-lossless with under 5% of KV, up to 5.8x throughput.
does_not_prove: CUDA kernels; slot reuse inside pages on Metal/vllm-metal not shown.
bearing: threatens: thought-aware reasoning KV compression; supports: block-level hole reuse port to Metal

title: ReasonCache: Accelerating Large Reasoning Model Serving through KV Cache Sharing
quote: LRMs frequently generate highly similar intermediate reasoning steps
proves: Similar reasoning steps produce similar KV; sharing it gives up to 89.2% peak and 40-60% average throughput gain.
does_not_prove: Approximate sharing; no prefix-exactness; not on device.
bearing: threatens: cross-request reasoning KV sharing

title: Understanding Inference Scaling for LLMs: Bottlenecks, Trade-offs, and Performance Principles
quote: KV-cache fragmentation forces early throttling resulting in sub-optimal compute utilization
proves: Long-output reasoning hits a KV capacity "reasoning cliff"; KV fragmentation causes early throttling.
does_not_prove: Abstract only; datacenter hardware; preemption details not in the abstract.
bearing: supports: decode-growth-aware admission/preemption on small memory

title: Qwen3-4B model card
quote: In multi-turn conversations, the historical model output should only include the final output part
proves: Qwen3's chat template drops prior turns' thinking content, so turn N+1's rendered prompt diverges from turn N's cached KV at the first stripped thinking block. Qwen3-4B: 36 layers, 32 Q heads, 8 KV heads, 32,768 native context.
does_not_prove: Card does not quantify the re-prefill cost; my inference is that the cached reasoning KV after the divergence point is wasted.
bearing: supports: gap on thinking-stripping vs prefix cache reuse (no paper found)

title: Together AI prompt caching docs
quote: The prefix is the prompt exactly as the model sees it, after the model's chat template renders your request into tokens.
proves: Prefix cache keys on the rendered template; reasoning and reasoning_effort settings are part of the prefix and changing them mid-conversation changes the rendered prompt.
does_not_prove: Provider doc; no numbers on how often reasoning templates cause misses.
bearing: supports: template-induced prefix invalidation for reasoning models

title: Marconi: Prefix Caching for the Era of Hybrid LLMs
quote: their use of in-place state updates for recurrent layers precludes rolling back cache entries for partial sequence overlaps
proves: Hybrid (SSM+attention) models only get exact-match prefix hits; reuse- and FLOP-aware admission/eviction gives up to 34.4x higher token hit rate (71.1% or 617 ms lower TTFT).
does_not_prove: GPU setting; predates vLLM align-mode checkpoints; not evaluated on Gated DeltaNet models or unified memory.
bearing: threatens: hybrid-model prefix cache admission; supports: checkpoint-interval tuning studies

title: vLLM design doc: Hybrid KV Cache Manager
quote: The core challenge is ensuring every layer type uses the same page size.
proves: vLLM groups layers by type, frees blocks outside sliding windows (round-robin buffers do not work with prefix caching), needs only the last window-1 tokens for an SWA hit, and forces one page size across attention and Mamba groups even though Mamba per-token state is much larger.
does_not_prove: Doc says Mamba prefix caching was work in progress at writing; no measurements of the page-size padding cost.
bearing: supports: page-size unification cost for hybrids; threatens: SWA block freeing as novel

title: vLLM docs: Automatic Prefix Caching (Mamba align mode)
quote: so a prefix-cache hit can resume only at a block boundary.
proves: Under --mamba-cache-mode align, Mamba state is checkpointed only on the Mamba block grid; an optional off-by-default shared-prefix checkpoint lets prefixes ending mid-block reuse state.
does_not_prove: No guidance on choosing the checkpoint grid; search snippet (unverified) reports Qwen3.5 attention block size 528 tokens so short prompts never hit.
bearing: supports: hybrid checkpoint granularity vs memory tradeoff as underexplored

title: vllm-metal v0.30.0 release notes
quote: Hybrid GDN prefix caching remains experimental
proves: On the user's stack: serving always uses paged attention; quantized --kv-cache-dtype (fp8, int8, nvfp4) rejected because Metal stores paged KV in model dtype; hybrid GDN prefix caching experimental with cache-on/off parity divergence; Nemotron-H and Granite 4.0 hybrid have prefix caching off.
does_not_prove: Release notes, not measurements; v0.31.0 state not checked.
bearing: supports: KV quantization in vllm-metal and hybrid prefix caching on Metal as open engineering gaps

title: Announcing vllm-metal: Concurrent Serving on Apple Silicon
quote: Requests that do not fit in the KV pool wait until pages become available.
proves: vllm-metal warms up then allocates the remaining --gpu-memory-utilization budget to a fixed KV pool, caps MLX buffer cache, leaves headroom for macOS; prefix caching reuses earlier turns; hybrid path cannot combine with speculative decoding.
does_not_prove: Fixed pool ignores changing OS memory pressure; no measurement of KV pool size vs macOS swapping.
bearing: supports: elastic KV pool under OS memory pressure on Mac (gap)

title: mlx-lm models/cache.py (KVCache, RotatingKVCache, ArraysCache, LRUPromptCache)
quote: return self.offset < self.max_size
proves: KVCache grows in steps of 256 tokens; RotatingKVCache is trimmable only before it wraps; ArraysCache (recurrent state) is never trimmable; can_trim_prompt_cache requires all layers trimmable; LRUPromptCache falls back to a shorter prefix when a longer entry cannot be trimmed, deep-copies on every read, evicts by count (default max_bytes 1<<63) balanced across system/user/assistant deques.
does_not_prove: Code reading only; no measurement of deep-copy cost or hit loss for hybrid/SWA models.
bearing: supports: checkpointed prefix cache for non-trimmable (hybrid, SWA) caches in mlx-lm; deep-copy cost on unified memory

title: mlx-lm server.py
quote: Maximum number of distinct KV caches to hold in the prompt cache
proves: mlx_lm.server prompt cache defaults to 10 entries with no byte limit unless --prompt-cache-bytes is set; batched path trims to budget left after active batch memory; chat prompts are split into system/user/assistant segments (and a small trailing thinking segment) for separate caching.
does_not_prove: Does not show behaviour under OS memory pressure.
bearing: supports: byte-aware or pressure-aware local prompt cache eviction

title: mlx-lm PR #1405: server: persist LRU prompt cache to disk across restarts
quote: the cache is lost on every server restart.
proves: Disk persistence of the mlx-lm prompt cache was proposed and closed unmerged on 2026-08-21 for review capacity, not on merit.
does_not_prove: No benchmark of restore cost vs re-prefill.
bearing: supports: SSD-backed prompt cache on Mac as unshipped in mlx-lm

title: llama.cpp PR #13194: kv-cache : add SWA support
quote: token information becomes lost when the window slides
proves: llama.cpp's window-sized SWA cache forgets old tokens on commit, so removing tokens or shifting positions is impossible; --swa-full falls back to a full-size cache.
does_not_prove: Does not measure prefix-reuse loss; later context-checkpoint mechanism not described here.
bearing: supports: SWA vs prefix reuse tradeoff on device

title: llama.cpp issue #24587: Context checkpoint invalidation loops with dynamic RAG prompts on SWA models (Qwen)
quote: deletes the checkpoint, and forces a full re-processing of the prompt.
proves: On SWA/hybrid Qwen3.5, changing middle content invalidates context checkpoints and forces full re-prefill even with an unchanged system prefix.
does_not_prove: Single user report, closed stale; no fix or measurement.
bearing: supports: checkpoint placement policy for SWA/hybrid local serving (gap)

title: gpt-oss-120b & gpt-oss-20b Model Card
quote: Each attention head has a learned bias in the denominator of the softmax.
proves: gpt-oss alternates banded-window (128 tokens) and dense attention layers, uses GQA with 8 KV heads, and has a learned per-head sink bias; half the layers need only 128 tokens of KV.
does_not_prove: No serving measurements; does not discuss prefix caching for windowed layers.
bearing: supports: mixed SWA/full block allocation studies

title: DeepSeek-V2 (MLA)
quote: MLA guarantees efficient inference through significantly compressing the Key-Value (KV) cache into a latent vector
proves: MLA stores one latent per token instead of per-head K/V; 93.3% KV reduction vs DeepSeek 67B.
does_not_prove: Says nothing about block size, paging, or offload tradeoffs once KV is 15x smaller; not relevant to Qwen3 models the user runs.
bearing: threatens: KV-size-driven ideas on MLA models; low bearing on Qwen3 testbed

title: Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct model card
quote: Hybrid Layout: 12 \* (3 \* (Gated DeltaNet -> MoE) -> 1 \* (Gated Attention -> MoE))
proves: Qwen3-Next: 48 layers, 3:1 Gated DeltaNet to gated attention, 2 KV heads, built-in MTP; only 12 layers keep growing KV.
does_not_prove: 80B model does not fit 16 GB; KV vs recurrent state sizes not given.
bearing: supports: hybrid state checkpoint studies (on smaller hybrids)

title: STree: Speculative Tree Decoding for Hybrid State-Space Models
quote: current SSMs lack the means to compute a token tree efficiently.
proves: Tree speculative decoding on SSM/hybrids is hard because recurrent state cannot be rolled back cheaply; STree uses accumulated state transition matrices to verify trees.
does_not_prove: Algorithmic; no interaction with prefix caching or paged state memory.
bearing: threatens: hybrid spec-decode rollback; supports: spec decode + hybrid prefix cache together (vllm-metal cannot combine them, F19)

title: KVBuffer: IO-aware Serving for Linear Attention
quote: increase the maximum number of serving requests by 5x for speculative decoding when verifying four draft tokens
proves: For linear-attention serving, keeping a temporary state per draft token is the memory cost of speculation; buffering draft KVs instead allows 5x more concurrent requests at 4 draft tokens.
does_not_prove: Linear attention only; no Apple hardware.
bearing: threatens: draft-state memory for hybrids

title: SpecMemo: Speculative Decoding is in Your Pocket
quote: minimizing redundant memory allocations for rejected candidate tokens
proves: Speculative decoding costs extra memory for candidate tokens; SpecMemo keeps 96% of speculative throughput on MT-Bench with 65% less generation memory.
does_not_prove: Titan RTX and MI250, not unified memory; no interaction with paged prefix cache.
bearing: threatens: draft-KV memory minimization

title: EAGLE-Pangu: Accelerator-Safe Tree Speculative Decoding on Ascend NPUs
quote: an explicit branch/commit cache manager built on the Cache API
proves: Tree speculation needs a branch/commit cache manager separating speculative branches from committed KV.
does_not_prove: Ascend-specific; no memory or block-size measurements in the abstract.
bearing: supports: branch/commit KV semantics on non-CUDA backends

title: KVSwap: Disk-aware KV Cache Offloading for Long-Context On-device Inference
quote: they are not suitable for embedded and mobile systems, where the CPU and GPU (or NPU) typically share a unified memory
proves: GPU-to-CPU KV offload is meaningless on unified memory; KVSwap keeps full KV on disk with compact in-memory metadata for preload prediction, giving higher throughput under tight memory budgets.
does_not_prove: Long-context single-request decode; not multi-turn prefix reuse or agent pauses.
bearing: threatens: SSD KV offload for long context on device; supports: SSD for cross-turn prefix retention

title: DynaKV: Enabling Accurate and Efficient Long-Sequence LLM Decoding on Smartphones
quote: KVCache distribution shifts render static or local cluster updates progressively misaligned
proves: Retrieval-based flash KV offload on phones degrades as KV distribution drifts during decoding; adaptive clusters give 1.38x accuracy and 1.47x speed.
does_not_prove: Phone flash; single-sequence decode.
bearing: threatens: retrieval KV on flash during long decode

title: mzCache: On-Device LLM Memory Management under Multitasking
quote: This creates memory pressure, forcing LLM memory (model weights and KV cache) to be evicted by the operating system.
proves: On multitasking phones the OS evicts weights and KV; fine-grained shared buffers with partial eviction/restoration give 2.1-5.5x lower TTFT than storage-backed partial offload.
does_not_prove: Phone OS (likely Android); macOS unified memory with wired limits and compressed memory not studied.
bearing: threatens: OS-pressure-aware KV on device; supports: macOS-specific version

title: LLM as a System Service on Mobile Devices
quote: LLMs execution often needs to maintain persistent states (mainly KV cache) across multiple invocations
proves: Treats one shared on-device LLM as a system service for many apps; chunk-wise KV compression and swapping cut context switch latency by up to 2 orders of magnitude.
does_not_prove: Mobile setting; no serving engine with paged KV and prefix sharing across apps.
bearing: threatens: multi-app shared model KV management

title: Agent Memory Below the Prompt: Persistent Q4 KV Cache for Multi-Agent LLM Inference on Edge Devices
quote: cache restoration reduces time-to-first-token by up to 136x
proves: Persisting each agent's KV to disk as 4-bit and reloading directly gives up to 136x TTFT reduction and fits 4x more agent contexts than FP16 (Apple hardware per search snippet).
does_not_prove: Single-author, self-reported; no comparison of eviction policies or TTL vs SSD tradeoff.
bearing: threatens: SSD-persisted agent KV on Mac; supports: rigorous break-even study

title: Native LLM and MLLM Inference at Scale on Apple Silicon (vllm-mlx)
quote: We implement LRU eviction to bound memory consumption, with configurable limits (default 512MB).
proves: vllm-mlx on Apple Silicon: prefix cache with LRU and 512 MB default limit; multimodal multi-turn latency 21.7s to 0.78s; KV need not move between devices on unified memory.
does_not_prove: No study of eviction policy, memory pressure or SSD tier.
bearing: supports: Apple-specific KV policy study is thin

title: Building py-kvcache: A Performance Characterization of External KV Caching for vLLM with NVMe SSDs
quote: External KV caching should therefore be treated as a setup specific admission decision.
proves: For short prefixes or fast GPUs recompute beats loading from external cache; on H100 the average Bailian-trace request is below break-even.
does_not_prove: H100 NVMe; the break-even on an M5 Air (slow compute, fast-ish SSD, shared memory) is unmeasured.
bearing: supports: SSD-vs-recompute break-even on laptops (gap); negative result for SSD tier on fast GPUs

title: oMLX guide (Better Stack)
quote: Older context and large static data like system prompts and tool definitions are frozen and moved to the SSD.
proves: A shipping Mac tool already tiers KV between unified memory and SSD for agents.
does_not_prove: Secondary write-up; no policy details or measurements.
bearing: threatens: novelty of SSD-tiered KV on Mac as engineering
